title: Summit and Passage
premise: Railroad engineer Freya Voss has spent three years mapping the closed mountain lines of a drowned borderland, measuring his life in miles since the war took everything else. When the river gives up a salvage chest stamped with the seal of the dead nation of Karelvo, he discovers the wreck of the Meridian Star — a train sunk with a fortune and a passenger list that includes his missing brother. Racing a ruthless salvage fleet led by the magnate Corvane Aldous, Freya assembles an unlikely crew of river people, deserters, and one defector from the fleet itself. In the flooded tunnels beneath Mount Serel, he learns the wreck's true cargo was evidence that could hang Aldous — and that his brother may have died protecting it. Freya surfaces with the truth and a found family bound tighter than blood, but only after paying the price of survival: the map, the miles, and the man he was before the river.
about_author: A. M. Nakamura is the pen name of a former surveyor who spent a decade charting decommissioned rail lines across three continents before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about the people history forgets to bury properly.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Freya Voss walks a closed mountain line at dawn, measuring trestles and recording distances in his battered ledger. Flashbacks reveal the war and his brother Tomas's disappearance three years ago. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: quiet grief disguised as routine; a man who has replaced time with distance.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: After a storm, Freya finds a waterlogged chest wedged in the riverbank, stamped with Karelvo's seal. Inside: a manifest for the sunken train Meridian Star — and Tomas's name on the crew list. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: shock cracking open three years of numbness.

chapters.title: The Salvage Fleet
chapters.summary: In the port town of Greyharbor, Freya learns magnate Corvane Aldous has already claimed the wreck by decree and launches in six tides. A dockworker named Sela tips him off that Aldous wants more than cargo. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: first taste of the machinery of power closing around him.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Freya studies the old maps and realizes the wreck lies beneath Mount Serel's flooded tunnels — reachable only through closed rail lines only he can navigate. He decides to race the fleet. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Crew of Strays
chapters.summary: Freya recruits Sela the smuggler, deserter diver Osk Brann, and engineer's apprentice Pip Wren, each carrying their own war debts. Their uneasy first night together around a fire. POV: rotating among the four. Emotional beat: the fragile first stitches of found family.

chapters.title: The Closed Line
chapters.summary: The crew reopens a sealed tunnel using Freya's engineering knowledge, nearly dying when a support fails. Osk saves Pip, earning grudging trust. POV: Pip. Emotional beat: fear becoming reliance; the crew stops being strangers.

chapters.title: Aldous Ascendant
chapters.summary: Cutaway to Aldous aboard his flagship dredger, bribing officials and discarding a subordinate who questioned the mission. We learn he served in Karelvo's final government. POV: Aldous. Emotional beat: cold charisma; power shown as appetite without limit.

chapters.title: The Defector
chapters.summary: Fleet navigator Ilsa Reyne defects to Freya's camp, bringing Aldous's dive schedule — but her motives are suspect, and Sela doesn't trust her. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: guilt and calculation; a woman trading one master for a chance at redemption.

chapters.title: Tide Against Tide
chapters.summary: A running chase on the river as the fleet's patrol skiff catches them; Sela's piloting and a rigged lock gate buy escape at the cost of their supplies. POV: Sela. Emotional beat: exhilaration shadowed by cost — survival is starting to take payment.

chapters.title: The Drowned Station
chapters.summary: The crew shelters in a submerged railway station, where Freya finds graffiti left by the Meridian Star's last crew — including a message signed T.V. Hope surges. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: grief and hope colliding; the brother becomes real again.

chapters.title: Pressure
chapters.summary: Osk trains the crew in diving basics while Ilsa reveals the wreck's cargo hold held sealed diplomatic cases, not gold. Frictions flare over whether to trust her. POV: Osk. Emotional beat: the team tested from within; loyalty must be chosen, not assumed.

chapters.title: The Fleet Arrives Early
chapters.summary: Aldous reaches Mount Serel two tides ahead of schedule, having tortured the location from a captured informant. The crew watches his floodlights bloom underwater. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: dread; the race is now a siege.

chapters.title: Through the Service Tunnel
chapters.summary: Freya leads the crew through a collapsing maintenance tunnel behind the fleet's position, using half-remembered blueprints. Pip nearly drowns; Freya carries her out. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: protective love crystallizing — these are his people now.

chapters.title: The Meridian Star
chapters.summary: They reach the tilted hulk of the train inside the flooded cavern. In the mail car, Freya finds Tomas's journal: his brother discovered Aldous's wartime treason and hid the evidence aboard. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: devastating revelation reframing everything.

chapters.title: What Tomas Knew
chapters.summary: Reading the journal by lamplight, the crew learns Aldous sold Karelvo's evacuation routes to enemy gunners — the disaster that killed thousands, including perhaps Tomas himself. POV: alternating Freya and Sela. Emotional beat: rage and mourning braided together.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Depth
chapters.summary: One crew member, desperate and bought, signals the fleet. Aldous's divers breach the cavern; Osk holds the tunnel door and is lost. POV: Osk, then Freya. Emotional beat: the price of survival comes due in blood; betrayal wounds deeper than enemies.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: Captured aboard the dredger, Freya is offered partnership and his brother's fate explained — Aldous claims Tomas drowned saving the evidence. Freya must choose wealth and silence or death and truth. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: temptation at its most seductive; corruption offered gently.

chapters.title: The Long Drop
chapters.summary: Sela and Pip stage a rescue, flooding a ballast compartment to force Aldous's crew to abandon ship sections. Freya escapes into the dark with the evidence case chained to his chest. POV: Sela. Emotional beat: ferocious, improvised courage; family fights like family.

chapters.title: Mount Serel Wakes
chapters.summary: The battle's explosives destabilize the cavern; the mountain begins to collapse as both crews flee the flooding tunnels. Aldous refuses to abandon the gold. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: nature indifferent to human greed; hubris meeting consequence.

chapters.title: The Last Tide
chapters.summary: In the collapsing tunnel, Freya confronts Aldous one-on-one. He offers him the evidence in exchange for letting the crew go — then triggers the flood that takes Aldous and the treasure together. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: climax; justice achieved at terrible personal cost.

chapters.title: Surface
chapters.summary: Four survivors drag themselves onto the riverbank as the mountain seals the wreck forever. Freya delivers the evidence to a journalist in Greyharbor, knowing it will burn his own name too. POV: Pip. Emotional beat: exhaustion, loss, and the stubborn persistence of truth.

chapters.title: Open Lines
chapters.summary: Months later, the crew repairs a dead branch line together, not for profit but because it connects isolated valley towns. Freya opens a new ledger and writes dates instead of miles. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: resolution; grief integrated, family chosen, life measured in years again.
